units.zh: 李常趙崔齊盧
units.en: Li, Chang, Zhao, Cui, Qi, and Lu
units.literal: Li, Chang, Zhao, Cui, Qi, Lu

units.zh: 李揆，字端卿，系出隴西，為冠族，去客滎陽。
units.en: Li Kui, whose style name was Duanqing, came from the eminent Longxi line and settled with his family as guests in Xingyang.
units.literal: Li Kui, style name Duanqing, traced his lineage to Longxi, was a leading clan, and went to live as guests in Xingyang.

units.zh: 祖玄道，為文學館學士。
units.en: His grandfather Xuandao had been a scholar at the Literature Institute.
units.literal: His grandfather Xuandao served as a scholar of the Literature Institute.

units.zh: 父成裕，秘書監。
units.en: His father Chengyu held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: His father Chengyu was Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 揆性警敏，善文章。
units.en: Kui was quick-witted by nature and excelled at literary composition.
units.literal: Kui by nature was alert and quick-witted and skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 開元末，擢進士第，補陳留尉。
units.en: Near the end of the Kaiyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Chenliu.
units.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he was selected in the jinshi examination and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Chenliu.

units.zh: 獻書闕下，試中書，遷右拾遺，再轉起居郎，知宗子表疏，以考功郎中知制誥。
units.en: He submitted writings to the court, passed the Secretariat examination, rose to Right Reminder, was transferred to Court Diarist in charge of imperial-clan memorials, and then drafted edicts as Director of Merit Evaluation.
units.literal: He presented writings at the court, passed the Secretariat examination, was promoted to Right Reminder, transferred to Court Diarist, managed imperial-clan memorials, and as Director of Merit Evaluation drafted edicts.

units.zh: 扈狩劍南，拜中書舍人。
units.en: When he accompanied the emperor's progress to Jiannan, he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
units.literal: When he accompanied the hunt to Sword South he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 乾元二年，宗室請上皇后號曰「翊聖」。
units.en: In the second year of Qianyuan, members of the imperial clan asked that the empress be given the honorific title "Assisting Sage."
units.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan the imperial clan requested that the empress be given the honorific title "Assisting Sage."

units.zh: 肅宗問揆，對曰：「前代後妃，終則有謚，景龍不君，韋氏專恣，乃稱翊聖。
units.en: Emperor Suzong asked Kui, who answered: "In earlier ages empresses and consorts received posthumous titles only after death. During the Jinglong years the throne went astray and the Wei clan seized unchecked power; only then was the title 'Assisting Sage' used.
units.literal: Emperor Suzong asked Kui, who replied: "Consorts of past dynasties received posthumous titles only after death. In the Jinglong era the ruler lost his way, and the Wei clan acted with unchecked arrogance—it was then that 'Assisting Sage' was used.

units.zh: 今陛下動遵典禮，奈何踵其亂哉？」
units.en: Your Majesty now follows the canonical rites in every move—why tread again the path of that disorder?"
units.literal: Now Your Majesty acts in accord with canonical ritual—why follow in the footsteps of that disorder?"

units.zh: 帝驚曰：「幾誤我家事。」
units.en: The emperor exclaimed in alarm: "I nearly ruined my own house."
units.literal: The emperor said in alarm: "I nearly brought ruin on my house."

units.zh: 遂止。
units.en: He dropped the matter.
units.literal: He then stopped.

units.zh: 後即張氏，有子數歲，欲立為太子，而帝意未決。
units.en: Later there was Lady Zhang, who had a son still only a few years old and wished to have him made heir apparent, but the emperor had not yet made up his mind.
units.literal: Later there was Lady Zhang, who had a son still young; she wished to have him established as heir apparent, but the emperor had not yet decided.

units.zh: 時代宗以封成王，帝從容語揆曰：「成王長，有功，將定太子，卿意謂何？」
units.en: At that time Daizong had been enfeoffed as Prince of Cheng. The emperor spoke to Kui in an easy tone: "The Prince of Cheng is grown, has merit, and I am about to settle the heir apparent—what do you think?"
units.literal: At that time Emperor Daizong had been enfeoffed as Prince of Cheng; the emperor spoke casually to Kui: "The Prince of Cheng is grown, has achievements, and will be made heir apparent—what is your view?"

units.zh: 揆曰：「陛下此言，社稷福也。」
units.en: Kui said: "Your Majesty's words are a blessing to the realm."
units.literal: Kui said: "Your Majesty's words are a blessing to the altars of state."

units.zh: 因再拜賀。
units.en: He then bowed twice in congratulation.
units.literal: Thereupon he bowed twice in congratulation.

units.zh: 帝曰：「朕計決矣。」
units.en: The emperor said: "My mind is made up."
units.literal: The emperor said: "I have settled the matter."

units.zh: 俄兼禮部侍郎。
units.en: Before long he was also made Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: Soon he was concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 揆病取士不考實，徒露搜索禁所挾，而迂學陋生，葄枕圖史，且不能自措於詞。
units.en: Kui faulted the selection of scholars for failing to test real ability: officials only exposed candidates who carried forbidden materials hidden in their robes, while pedantic, shallow students who had slept with histories and maps under their pillows could not even put words in order.
units.literal: Kui was ill with selecting scholars without examining their true abilities, merely exposing those who carried illicit materials from the forbidden quarters in their robes, while pedantic and shallow students who had pillowed their heads on charts and histories could not even manage words.

units.zh: 乃大陳書廷中，進諸儒約曰：「上選士，第務得才，可盡所欲言。」
units.en: He then spread books widely in the court hall, summoned the candidates forward, and declared: "When the sovereign chooses scholars, he seeks only talent; say everything you wish."
units.literal: He then arrayed books extensively in the court, advanced the scholar-officials, and declared: "When the sovereign selects scholars, he seeks only to obtain talent—you may all say what you will."

units.zh: 由是人人稱美。
units.en: From this everyone praised him.
units.literal: Because of this everyone praised him.

units.zh: 未卒事，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，修國史，封姑臧縣伯。
units.en: Before the examination was finished he was appointed Vice President of the Secretariat and Co-Chancellor, put in charge of compiling the national history, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guzang.
units.literal: Before the matter was finished he was appointed Vice President of the Secretariat, Co-Chancellor, compiled the national history, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guzang.

units.zh: 揆美風儀，善奏對，帝嘆曰：「卿門地、人物、文學皆當世第一，信朝廷羽儀乎！」
units.en: Kui had a handsome presence and answered memorials with skill. The emperor sighed and said: "Your family standing, person, and literary learning are all first in the age—you are truly the court's ceremonial wings!"
units.literal: Kui had fine bearing and was skilled at memorial replies; the emperor sighed and said: "Your family standing, person, and literary learning are all first in this age—you are truly the ceremonial wings of the court!

units.zh: 故時稱三絕。
units.en: He was therefore called the "triple surpassing" of the age.
units.literal: Therefore he was then called the "triple surpassing."

units.zh: 於是京師多盜，至驂衢殺人，屍溝中，吏褫氣。
units.en: At that time bandits were numerous in the capital; they killed people even in the main thoroughfares, corpses choked the ditches, and officials lost heart.
units.literal: At this time there were many bandits in the capital; they killed people even in the broad streets, corpses filled the ditches, and officials lost their spirit.

units.zh: 李輔國方橫，請選羽林騎五百，備僥捕。
units.en: Li Fuguo was then riding high in power and asked to select five hundred imperial guard horsemen for rash pursuit and arrest.
units.literal: Li Fuguo was then domineering and requested to select five hundred imperial guard cavalry for opportunistic arrests.

units.zh: 揆曰：「漢以南、北軍相統攝，故周勃因南軍入北軍，以安劉氏。
units.en: Kui said: "Under the Han the Southern and Northern Armies kept each other in check; that is why Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern Army and thereby secured the house of Liu.
units.literal: Kui said: "In Han times the Southern and Northern Armies checked each other, so Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern Army and thereby secured the Liu house.

units.zh: 本朝置南、北衙，文武區別，更相檢伺。
units.en: Our dynasty set up Southern and Northern courts, separating civil and military so that each inspected the other.
units.literal: Our dynasty established Southern and Northern courts, separating civil and military, each inspecting the other.

units.zh: 今以羽林代金吾，忽有非常，何以制之！」
units.en: If the imperial guard cavalry now replace the Jinwu guard, and something unforeseen should occur, how would it be controlled?"
units.literal: Now to use the imperial guard cavalry in place of the Jinwu guard—if something unforeseen should arise, how would it be controlled?"

units.zh: 輔國議格。
units.en: Fuguo's proposal was blocked.
units.literal: Fuguo's proposal was blocked.

units.zh: 揆決事明當，然銳於進，且近名。
units.en: Kui's decisions were clear and apt, but he was keen to advance and fond of reputation.
units.literal: Kui's decisions were clear and appropriate, but he was sharp in advancement and fond of reputation.

units.zh: 兄楷，有時稱，滯冗官不得遷。
units.en: His elder brother Kai enjoyed a contemporary reputation but languished in idle posts and could not win promotion.
units.literal: His elder brother Kai had a contemporary reputation but languished in redundant posts and could not be promoted.

units.zh: 呂諲政事出揆遠甚，以故宰相鎮荊南，治聲尤高。
units.en: Lu Yun's handling of affairs far outshone Kui's; as a former chancellor posted to Jingnan, his reputation for governance was especially high.
units.literal: Lu Yun's administration far surpassed Kui's; as a former chancellor governing Jingnan his renown for governance was especially great.

units.zh: 揆懼復用，遣吏至諲所，構抉過失，諲密訴諸朝。
units.en: Kui feared Yun would be brought back into office, sent officials to his post to fabricate and expose faults, and Yun secretly appealed to the court.
units.literal: Kui feared his reappointment, dispatched officials to Yun's post to contrive and expose his faults, and Yun secretly lodged complaints at court.

units.zh: 帝怒，貶揆袁州長史。
units.en: The emperor was enraged and demoted Kui to Chief Administrator of Yuan Prefecture.
units.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Kui to Chief Administrator of Yuan Prefecture.

units.zh: 不三日，以楷為司門員外郎。
units.en: Within three days Kai was appointed Vice Director of the Gate Office.
units.literal: Within three days Kai was made Vice Director of the Gate Office.

units.zh: 揆累年乃徙歙州刺史。
units.en: Only after many years was Kui transferred to prefect of She Prefecture.
units.literal: Only after many years was Kui transferred to Prefect of She Prefecture.

units.zh: 初，苗晉卿數薦元載，揆輕載地寒，謂晉卿曰：「龍章鳳姿士不見用，獐頭鼠目子乃求官邪？」
units.en: Earlier Miao Jinqing had repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai. Kui looked down on Zai's humble origins and said to Jinqing: "Men of dragon bearing and phoenix grace go unused, yet a weasel-headed, rat-eyed fellow seeks office?"
units.literal: Earlier Miao Jinqing had repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai; Kui looked down on Zai's humble origins and said to Jinqing: "A dragon-marked, phoenix-bearing gentleman is not employed, yet a weasel-headed, rat-eyed fellow seeks office?"

units.zh: 載聞，銜之。
units.en: When Zai heard this he bore a grudge.
units.literal: When Zai heard this he harbored resentment.

units.zh: 及秉政，奏揆試秘書監，江淮養疾。
units.en: When he came to power he had Kui appointed on probation as Director of the Secretariat and sent to convalesce in the Jianghuai region.
units.literal: When he came to power he memorialized that Kui be tried as Director of the Secretariat and convalesce in Jianghuai.

units.zh: 家百口，貧無祿，丐食取給，牧守稍厭慁，則去之，流落凡十六年。
units.en: His household of a hundred mouths had no stipend and lived by begging; when local governors grew tired of their importuning they moved on. In all he wandered for sixteen years.
units.literal: His household of a hundred mouths had no salary; they begged food to sustain themselves; when governors grew weary of their complaints they left, and he wandered in all for sixteen years.

units.zh: 載誅，始拜睦州刺史。
units.en: After Zai was executed he was at last appointed prefect of Mu Prefecture.
units.literal: When Zai was executed he was at last appointed Prefect of Mu Prefecture.

units.zh: 入為國子祭酒、禮部尚書。
units.en: He was recalled to the capital as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 德宗幸山南，揆素為盧杞所惡，用為入蕃會盟使，拜尚書左仆射。
units.en: When Emperor Dezong went to the south of the mountains, Kui had long been hated by Lu Qi, who sent him as envoy to the barbarians for a treaty alliance and had him appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Emperor Dezong went to the south of the mountains, Kui had long been hated by Lu Qi; Qi used him as envoy for a treaty alliance with the barbarians, with the title of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 揆辭老，恐死道路，不能達命，帝惻然。
units.en: Kui pleaded old age, saying he feared he would die on the road and fail to carry out the mission. The emperor was moved to pity.
units.literal: Kui pleaded old age, fearing death on the road and inability to fulfil the decree; the emperor was moved to compassion.

units.zh: 杞曰：「和戎者，當練朝廷事，非揆不可。
units.en: Qi said: "One who makes peace with the barbarians must be versed in court affairs; no one but Kui will do.
units.literal: Qi said: "One who harmonizes with the barbarians must be versed in court affairs—no one but Kui will do.

units.zh: 異時年少揆者不敢辭。」
units.en: At another time a man younger than Kui would not have dared refuse."
units.literal: At another time a man younger than Kui would not have dared refuse.

units.zh: 揆至蕃，酋長曰：「聞唐有第一人李揆，公是否？」
units.en: When Kui reached the barbarians the chieftain said: "I have heard that Tang has a foremost man named Li Kui—is that you?"
units.literal: When Kui reached the barbarian realm the chieftain said: "I hear Tang has a foremost man Li Kui—is that you?"

units.zh: 揆畏留，因紿之曰：「彼李揆，安肯來邪？」
units.en: Kui feared being detained and deceived him, saying: "That Li Kui—how would he be willing to come?"
units.literal: Kui feared detention and deceived him, saying: "That Li Kui—how would he be willing to come?"

units.zh: 還。
units.en: He returned.
units.literal: He returned.

units.zh: 卒鳳州，年七十四，贈司空，謚曰恭。
units.en: He died at Feng Prefecture at the age of seventy-four, was posthumously made Director of Works, and given the posthumous name Gong.
units.literal: He died at Feng Prefecture at seventy-four, was posthumously awarded Director of Works, posthumous name Gong.

units.zh: 常袞，京兆人，天寶末，及進士第。
units.en: Chang Gun was a man of Jingzhao. At the end of the Tianbao reign he passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: Chang Gun, a man of Jingzhao, at the end of Tianbao passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 性狷潔，不妄交遊。
units.en: By nature he was fastidious and aloof and did not associate casually.
units.literal: By nature he was narrow and fastidious and did not associate casually.

units.zh: 由太子正字，累為中書舍人。
units.en: Starting as Rectifier of Records in the Heir Apparent's palace, he rose through several posts to Secretariat Drafter.
units.literal: From Rectifier of Records in the Heir Apparent's palace he rose through several posts to Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 文采贍蔚，長於應用，譽重一時。
units.en: His literary talent was rich and abundant, he excelled at practical composition, and his reputation weighed heavily in the age.
units.literal: His literary talent was rich and abundant, skilled in practical application, and his reputation weighed heavily in the age.

units.zh: 魚朝恩賴寵，兼判國子監。
units.en: Yu Chaoen relied on imperial favor and concurrently directed the Directorate of Education.
units.literal: Yu Chaoen relied on favor and concurrently held the Directorship of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 袞奏：「成均之任，當用名儒，不宜以宦臣領職。」
units.en: Gun memorialized: "The charge of the Exalted Harmony institution should be given to renowned Confucians; it is not fitting that a eunuch official hold the post."
units.literal: Gun memorialized: "The charge of the Exalted Harmony institution should employ renowned Confucians; it is not fitting that a eunuch officer hold the post."

units.zh: 始，回紇有戰功者，得留京師，虜性易驕，後乃創邸第、佛祠，或伏甲其間，數出中渭橋，與軍人格鬥，奪含光門魚契走城外。
units.en: At first Uighur warriors with battle achievements were allowed to remain in the capital. Barbarians are easily made arrogant; later they built mansions and Buddhist shrines, sometimes hiding armed men within. Several times they came out at the Zhongwei Bridge, fought with soldiers, seized the Heguang Gate tally, and fled outside the walls.
units.literal: Initially Uighur warriors with battle achievements could remain in the capital; barbarian nature is easily arrogant; later they founded mansion compounds and Buddhist shrines, sometimes installing hidden arms within—several times they emerged at the Zhongwei Bridge, fought with soldiers, seized the Heguang Gate fish tally and fled outside the walls.

units.zh: 袞建言：「今西蕃盤桓境上，數入寇，若相連結，以乘無備，其變不細，請早圖之。」
units.en: Gun proposed: "The western barbarians now linger at the borders and raid repeatedly. If they join forces to strike when we are unprepared, the consequences would be grave. Please plan for this early."
units.literal: Gun proposed: "Now the western barbarians linger at the border and often raid in—if they join forces to exploit our lack of preparedness the change would not be slight; please plan for this early."

units.zh: 又天子誕日，諸道爭以侈麗奉獻，不則為老子、浮屠解禱事。
units.en: Moreover, on the emperor's birthday the various circuits vied to present lavish gifts; otherwise they offered prayers through Laozi and the Buddha.
units.literal: Also on the emperor's birthday the various circuits vied to present lavish gifts; otherwise they offered prayers through Laozi and the Buddha.

units.zh: 袞以為：「漢文帝還千里馬不用，晉武帝焚雉頭裘，宋高祖碎琥珀枕，是三主者，非有聰明大聖以致治安，謹身率下而已。
units.en: Gun argued: "Emperor Wen of Han sent back a thousand-li horse and would not use it; Emperor Wu of Jin burned the pheasant-head fur robe; Emperor Gaozu of Song smashed the amber pillow. These three rulers did not owe their peace and order to surpassing wisdom and sagacity; they simply guarded themselves and led those below by example.
units.literal: Gun held: "Emperor Wen of Han would not use a thousand-li horse sent back, Emperor Wu of Jin burned the pheasant-head fur robe, Emperor Gaozu of Song smashed the amber pillow—these three rulers were not possessed of surpassing wisdom and sagacity to attain good order; they merely guarded themselves and led those below.

units.zh: 今諸道饋獻，皆淫侈不急，而節度使、刺史非能男耕而女織者，類出於民，是斂怨以媚上也，請皆還之。
units.en: The gifts sent from the circuits today are all licentious extravagances of no urgency. Military commissioners and prefects are not men who plough and women who weave; for the most part the cost comes from the people. This is collecting resentment to flatter the throne. Please have them all returned.
units.literal: Now the presents from the circuits are all licentious extravagances without urgency; circuit military commissioners and prefects are not those who plough as men and weave as women—for the most part it comes from the people; this is collecting resentment to flatter the sovereign—please have them all returned.

units.zh: 今軍旅未寧，王畿戶口十不一在，而諸祠寺寫經造像，焚幣埋玉，所以賞賚若比丘、道士、巫祝之流，歲巨萬計。
units.en: The armies are not yet at peace, and scarcely one household in ten remains in the metropolitan region, yet shrines and temples copy sutras and cast images, burn silk offerings and bury jade. Rewards to Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, shamans, and the like amount to tens of thousands each year.
units.literal: Now the armies are not yet pacified, the population of the metropolitan region is not one in ten of what it was, yet the various shrines and temples copy sutras and cast images, burn silk and bury jade—the rewards to Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, shamans and the like run to tens of thousands each year.

units.zh: 陛下若以易芻粟，減貧民之賦，天下之福豈有量哉！」
units.en: If Your Majesty exchanged these for grain and fodder and reduced the levies on the poor, would the realm's blessings not be beyond measure!"
units.literal: If Your Majesty would exchange these for grass and grain and reduce the levies on the impoverished people, would the blessings of the realm not be beyond measure!"

units.zh: 代宗嘉納。
units.en: Emperor Daizong praised and adopted his advice.
units.literal: Emperor Daizong praised and adopted this.

units.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。
units.en: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 時宦者劉忠翼權震中外，涇原節度使馬璘為帝寵任，有所幹請，袞皆拒卻。
units.en: At that time the eunuch Liu Zhongyi's power shook court and countryside alike, and Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin enjoyed the emperor's favor. Whatever they requested, Gun refused.
units.literal: At that time the eunuch Liu Zhongyi's authority shook inside and outside; Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin was the emperor's favored appointee—whatever they requested Gun refused.

units.zh: 元載死，拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，弘文、崇文館大學士，與楊綰同執政。
units.en: When Yuan Zai died he was appointed Vice President of the Secretariat and Co-Chancellor, made Grand Academician of the Hongwen and Chongwen halls, and governed together with Yang Guan.
units.literal: When Yuan Zai died he was made Vice President of the Secretariat, Co-Chancellor, Grand Academician of the Hongwen and Chongwen halls, governing together with Yang Guan.

units.zh: 綰長厚通可，而袞苛細，以清儉自賢。
units.en: Guan was generous and easy to work with, but Gun was exacting in detail and made frugality his claim to virtue.
units.literal: Guan was generous and accommodating, but Gun was exacting in detail and made frugality his virtue.

units.zh: 帝內重綰而顓任之，禮遇信愛，袞弗及也，每所恨忌。
units.en: The emperor valued Guan inwardly and entrusted affairs to him alone, treating him with trust and affection that Gun never matched; at every turn Gun nursed resentment.
units.literal: The emperor valued Guan inwardly and entrusted affairs exclusively to him, treating him with trust and affection that Gun did not attain; at each turn he harbored resentment.

units.zh: 會綰卒，袞始當國。
units.en: When Guan died, Gun at last held the reins of government.
units.literal: When Guan died Gun at last held the state.

units.zh: 先是，百官俸寡狹，議增給之。
units.en: Earlier the salaries of the hundred officials had been meager and narrow, and there was discussion of increasing them.
units.literal: Earlier the salaries of the hundred officials were meager and narrow; they discussed increasing them.

units.zh: 時韓滉使度支，與袞皆任情輕重。
units.en: At that time Han Huang handled the office of revenue; he and Gun both adjusted amounts as they pleased.
units.literal: At that time Han Huang handled the office of revenue and, with Gun, both gauged weight as they pleased.

units.zh: 滉惡國子司業張參，袞惡太子少詹事趙惎，皆少給之。
units.en: Huang hated Zhang Can, Vice Director of the Directorate; Gun hated Zhao Ji, the Heir Apparent's Junior Administrator. Both men received reduced stipends.
units.literal: Huang hated the Vice Director of the Directorate Zhang Can; Gun hated the Heir Apparent's Junior Administrator Zhao Ji—both received less.

units.zh: 太子文學為洗馬副，袞姻家任文學者，其給乃在洗馬上。
units.en: The Heir Apparent's literary instructor ranked below the groom of the heir apparent, but Gun's relative by marriage held the literary instructor post and received a stipend higher than the groom's.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent's literary instructor was deputy groom of the heir apparent; Gun's affinal relative held the literary instructor post—his stipend was actually above the groom's.

units.zh: 其騁私崇怨類此。
units.en: His pursuit of private interest and accumulation of grievances were of this kind.
units.literal: His pursuit of private interest and heaping up of grievances were of this kind.

units.zh: 故事，日出內廚食賜宰相家，可十人具，袞奏罷之。
units.en: By precedent, at sunrise food from the inner kitchen was sent to the chancellor's household for ten persons. Gun memorialized to abolish the practice.
units.literal: By precedent at sunrise food from the inner kitchen was bestowed on the chancellor's household for ten persons; Gun memorialized to abolish this.

units.zh: 又將讓堂封，它宰相不從，乃止。
units.en: He was also about to decline the Hall sealing stipend, but the other chancellors would not agree, and the matter was dropped.
units.literal: He was also about to decline the Hall sealing, but other chancellors would not agree and it was stopped.

units.zh: 政事堂北門，異時宰相過舍人院咨逮政事，至袞乃塞之，以示尊大。
units.en: The northern gate of the Administration Hall: in former times chancellors passed through the drafters' courtyard to consult on affairs of state; only under Gun was it blocked, to display his loftiness.
units.literal: The northern gate of the Administration Hall—in former times chancellors passed through the drafters' courtyard to consult on administration; only under Gun was it blocked to display loftiness.

units.zh: 懲元載敗，窒賣官之路，然一切以公議格之，非文詞者皆擯不用，故世謂之「濌伯」，以其濌々無賢不肖之辨雲。
units.en: Punishing Yuan Zai's fall, he blocked the sale of offices, yet he rejected everything by public discussion. Those without literary skill were all cast aside unused. The age therefore called him "Sloppy Uncle," because he sloppily made no distinction between the worthy and the unworthy.
units.literal: Punishing Yuan Zai's defeat he blocked the sale of offices route, yet he rejected everything by public discussion—those without literary skill were all banished unused; therefore the age called him "Sloppy Uncle," because he sloppily distinguished no worthy from unworthy.

units.zh: 袞為相，散官才朝議，而無封爵，郭子儀言於帝，遂加銀青光祿大夫，封河內郡公。
units.en: As chancellor Gun held only the scattered post of Chaoyi and had no enfeoffment. Guo Ziyi spoke to the emperor, and Gun was then given the rank of Silver-Green-Ware Glory Grandee and enfeoffed as Duke of Henei.
units.literal: Gun as chancellor held only the scattered post of Chaoyi and had no enfeoffment; Guo Ziyi spoke to the emperor, and he was then added Silver-Green-Ware Glory Grandee and enfeoffed Duke of Henei.

units.zh: 德宗即位，袞奏貶崔祐甫為河南少尹。
units.en: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Gun memorialized to demote Cui Youfu to Vice Governor of Henan.
units.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne Gun memorialized to demote Cui Youfu to Vice Governor of Henan.

units.zh: 帝怒，使與祐甫換秩，再貶潮州刺史。
units.en: The emperor was angry, had him exchange ranks with Youfu, and demoted him again to prefect of Chaozhou.
units.literal: The emperor was angry, had him exchange ranks with Youfu, and demoted him again to Prefect of Chaozhou.

units.zh: 建中初，楊炎輔政，起為福建觀察使。
units.en: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, when Yang Yan came to power, Gun was appointed Fujian Observation Commissioner.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Yang Yan came to power and Gun was appointed Fujian Observation Commissioner.

units.zh: 始，閩人未知學，袞至，為設鄉校，使作為文章，親加講導，與為客主鈞禮，觀遊燕饗與焉，由是俗一變，歲貢士與內州等。
units.en: At first the people of Min had not yet taken to learning. When Gun arrived he established village schools, had them compose essays, and personally lectured and guided them. He treated them with the equal ceremony of host and guest, attended their outings, banquets, and feasts, and thereby changed the local customs entirely. Each year the scholars they presented for examination equalled those of the inner circuits.
units.literal: Initially the people of Min did not yet know learning; when Gun arrived he established village schools, had them compose essays, personally lectured and guided them, treated them as guest and host with equal ceremony, attended their tours, banquets and feasts—for this the customs changed entirely, and each year scholars presented for examination equalled those of inner circuits.

units.zh: 卒於官，年五十五，贈尚書左仆射。
units.en: He died in office at the age of fifty-five and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: He died in office at fifty-five, posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 其後閩人春秋配享袞於學官雲。
units.en: Thereafter the people of Min sacrificed to Gun at the learning hall in spring and autumn.
units.literal: Thereafter the people of Min in spring and autumn sacrificed to Gun at the learning hall.

units.zh: 趙憬，字退翁，渭州隴西人。
units.en: Zhao Jing, whose style name was Tuiweng, was a man of Longxi in Weizhou.
units.literal: Zhao Jing, style name Tuiweng, a man of Longxi in Weizhou.

units.zh: 曾祖仁本，仕為吏部侍郎、同東西臺三品。
units.en: His great-grandfather Renben had served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Co-Director of the Eastern and Western Platforms at the third rank.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Renben held the offices of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Co-Director of the Eastern and Western Platforms, Third Rank.

units.zh: 憬誌行峻潔，不自衒賈。
units.en: Jing's will and conduct were stern and pure; he did not parade himself for gain.
units.literal: Jing's will and conduct were stern and pure; he did not parade himself for sale.

units.zh: 寶應中，方營泰、建二陵，用度廣，又吐蕃盜邊，天下薦饑，憬褐衣上疏，請殺禮從儉，士林嘆美。
units.en: During the Baoying period work was underway on the Taizong and Jianling mausoleums with heavy expenditures, Tibet raided the borders, and famine spread across the realm. Jing submitted a memorial in plain dress asking that rites be cut back and thrift observed. Scholars sighed in admiration.
units.literal: In the Baoying period they were constructing the Tai and Jian mausoleums with broad expenditures; also Tibet raided the border; famine spread across the realm; Jing in plain dress submitted a memorial requesting reduction of rites and thrift—the scholarly world sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 試江夏尉，佐諸使府，進太子舍人。
units.en: He was tested as assistant magistrate of Jiangxia, served in several commissioner offices, and advanced to Cadet of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He was tested as Assistant Magistrate of Jiangxia, assisted various commissioner offices, and advanced to Cadet of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 母喪免，有芝生壤樹。
units.en: When his mother died he left office; auspicious fungi grew on the mound tree at her grave.
units.literal: When his mother died he left office; fungi grew on the mound tree at the grave.

units.zh: 建中初，擢水部員外郎。
units.en: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was promoted to Vice Director of the Water Office.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was promoted to Vice Director of the Water Office.

units.zh: 湖南觀察使李承表憬自副。
units.en: Hunan Observation Commissioner Li Cheng recommended Jing as his own deputy.
units.literal: Hunan Observation Commissioner Li Cheng recommended Jing as his deputy.

units.zh: 承卒，遂代之。
units.en: When Cheng died, Jing replaced him.
units.literal: When Cheng died Jing replaced him.

units.zh: 召還，闔門不與人交。
units.en: When he was summoned back to the capital he shut his gate and would not receive visitors.
units.literal: Summoned back, he shut his gate and did not meet people.

units.zh: 李泌薦之，對殿中，占奏明辯，通古今，德宗欽悅，拜給事中。
units.en: Li Mi recommended him. When he faced the emperor in the hall his memorial replies were clear and eloquent and showed mastery of antiquity and the present. Emperor Dezong was deeply pleased and appointed him Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: Li Mi recommended him; facing the emperor in the hall his memorial delivery was clear and eloquent, penetrating antiquity and the present; Emperor Dezong was deeply pleased and appointed him Drafting Attendant.

units.zh: 貞元中，鹹安公主降回紇，詔關播為使，而憬以御史中丞副之。
units.en: During the Zhenyuan period Princess Xian'an was married to the Uighurs. The emperor ordered Guan Bo as envoy, with Jing serving as deputy in the rank of Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the Zhenyuan period Princess Xian'an was married to the Uighurs; the emperor ordered Guan Bo as envoy, with Jing as deputy in the rank of Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 異時使者多私賫，以市馬規利入，獨憬不然。
units.en: On previous missions envoys had often carried private gifts to buy horses and skim profits for themselves; Jing alone refused to do so.
units.literal: In other times envoys often privately brought tribute gifts, using them to buy horses and scheme for profit entering [their pockets]; Jing alone was not so.

units.zh: 使未還，尚書左丞缺，帝曰：「趙憬堪此。」
units.en: Before the mission returned, the post of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat fell vacant. The emperor said: "Zhao Jing is suited to it."
units.literal: The envoy had not yet returned; the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat post was vacant. The emperor said: "Zhao Jing is fit for this."

units.zh: 遂以命之。
units.en: He thereupon gave him the appointment.
units.literal: He thereupon appointed him.

units.zh: 考功歲終，請如至德故事課殿最，憬自言薦果州刺史韋證，以貪敗，請降考。
units.en: At the year's end the Directorate of Merit Review asked to rank offices by performance as in the Zhide precedent. Jing himself reported that he had recommended Wei Zheng, prefect of Guo Prefecture, who had been ruined by greed, and asked that his own evaluation be lowered.
units.literal: At year-end the Directorate of Merit Review requested grading offices by best and worst per the Zhide precedent. Jing himself said he had recommended Guo Prefecture Prefect Wei Zheng, who failed through corruption, and requested lowering his own grade.

units.zh: 校考使劉滋謂憬知過，更以考升。
units.en: The collation review commissioner Liu Zi said that because Jing recognized his error, he raised his grade instead.
units.literal: The collation review commissioner Liu Zi said Jing knew his fault and instead raised his grade.

units.zh: 竇參當國，欲抑為刺史，帝不許。
units.en: While Dou Can held power he tried to have Jing reduced to a prefect, but the emperor refused.
units.literal: When Dou Can controlled the state he wished to demote [Jing] to prefect; the emperor did not permit it.

units.zh: 參罷，進中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，與陸贄同輔政。
units.en: After Can was dismissed, Jing was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, sharing governance with Lu Zhi.
units.literal: When Can was dismissed, [Jing] was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, assisting in governance together with Lu Zhi.

units.zh: 贄於裁決少所讓，又徙憬門下侍郎，繇是不平。
units.en: Zhi seldom gave way in policy decisions, and Jing was further transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery; from this Jing grew resentful.
units.literal: Zhi in decisions rarely yielded; [Jing] was also moved to Vice Director of the Chancellery—from this [Jing] was discontent.

units.zh: 自以不任職，數稱疾。
units.en: Believing himself unequal to the post, he repeatedly pleaded illness.
units.literal: Considering himself unfit for office, he repeatedly claimed illness.

units.zh: 時杜黃裳遭奄人讒詆，穆贊、韋武、李宣、盧雲等為裴延齡構擯，勢危甚，憬救護申解，皆得免。
units.en: At the time Du Huangshang was slandered by eunuchs, and Mu Zan, Wei Wu, Li Xuan, Lu Yun, and others were framed and driven out by Pei Yanling until their situation was dire. Jing intervened on their behalf and secured their release.
units.literal: At the time Du Huangshang suffered slander by eunuchs; Mu Zan, Wei Wu, Li Xuan, Lu Yun, and others were framed and ousted by Pei Yanling—their peril was extreme. Jing rescued and pleaded on their behalf, and all were spared.

units.zh: 初，贄約共執退延齡，既對，贄極言其奸，帝色變，憬不為助，遂罷贄，乃始當國。
units.en: At first Zhi and Jing had agreed to join forces to remove Yanling. When they faced the throne, Zhi denounced Yanling's treachery at length until the emperor's face changed, but Jing offered no support. Zhi was dismissed, and only then did Jing take control of the government.
units.literal: Initially Zhi agreed with [Jing] to jointly move to remove Yanling. Once they faced the emperor, Zhi spoke at length of his wickedness; the emperor's expression changed; Jing did not assist—thus Zhi was dismissed, and only then [Jing] began to control the state.

units.zh: 憬精治道，常以國本在選賢、節用、薄賦斂、寬刑罰，懇懇為天子言之。
units.en: Jing was deeply versed in statecraft and repeatedly urged the emperor, with great earnestness, that the nation's foundation rested on choosing worthy men, curbing expenditure, keeping taxes light, and moderating punishments.
units.literal: Jing was well versed in the art of governance. He constantly told the Son of Heaven in earnest that the foundation of the state lay in selecting the worthy, economizing expenditure, light taxation, and lenient punishments.

units.zh: 又陳前世損益、當時之變，獻《審官六議》。
units.en: He also reviewed what earlier ages had gained and lost and what the present age required, submitting his Six Discourses on Examining Office.
units.literal: He also set forth the gains and losses of former ages and the changes of the present time, presenting the Six Discourses on Examining Office.

units.zh: 一議相臣，曰：「中外知其賢者用之，能者任之，責材之備，為不可得。」
units.en: The first discourse, on the chief minister, said: "At court and in the provinces, appoint men known to be worthy and assign men known to be capable. To demand fully rounded talent in every case is impossible."
units.literal: The first discourse on the chief minister said: "Within and without, employ those known as worthy and assign those who are capable. To require a full endowment of talent is impossible to obtain."

units.zh: 二議庶官，曰：「臣嘗謂拔十得五，賢愚猶半。
units.en: The second discourse, on common officials, said: "I once argued that if you select ten men and get five good ones, the wise and the foolish are still evenly split.
units.literal: The second discourse on common officials said: "Your servant once said that from ten selections five would prove good—the worthy and the foolish would still be half and half.

units.zh: 陛下曰：『何必五也，十二可矣。』
units.en: Your Majesty replied: 'Why insist on half? One or two good men from ten would be enough.'
units.literal: Your Majesty said: 'Why need five? One or two from ten would suffice.'

units.zh: 故廣任用，明殿最，舉大節，略小瑕，隨能試事，用人之大要也。」
units.en: So the great principle of employing men is to appoint broadly, distinguish clearly between the best and the worst, honor major integrity, overlook small faults, and test each man according to his ability."
units.literal: Therefore broadly employ men, clearly distinguish best and worst, promote great integrity, overlook minor flaws, and test them according to ability—this is the great principle of employing men."

units.zh: 三議京司闕官，曰：「今要官闕多，閑官員多。
units.en: The third discourse, on vacant offices in the capital, said: "Important posts stand empty in great numbers, while idle posts are filled in great numbers.
units.literal: The third discourse on vacant capital offices said: "Now important posts have many vacancies, while idle posts have many incumbents.

units.zh: 要官以材行，閑官以恩澤，是選拔少，優容眾也。
units.en: Important posts go to men of talent and character, while idle posts go to men of favor. That means too little selection and too much accommodation.
units.literal: Important posts are filled by talent and conduct; idle posts by favor—this means few selections and indulgence of the many.

units.zh: 宜補缺員，以育人材。」
units.en: Vacant posts should be filled so that talent may be cultivated."
units.literal: Vacancies should be filled to cultivate talent."

units.zh: 四議考課，曰：「今內庶僚，外刺史，課最尤者，擢以不次，善矣。
units.en: The fourth discourse, on performance review, said: "Today, among inner officials and outer prefects alike, those with the highest marks are promoted ahead of schedule, and that is well.
units.literal: The fourth discourse on evaluation said: "Now for inner common officials and outer prefects, those with the highest evaluation grades are promoted out of turn—this is good.

units.zh: 臣謂黜陟宜責歲限，若任要重未當遷者，加爵或秩。
units.en: I hold that promotions and demotions should follow fixed terms of years. If a man holds a weighty post and is not yet due to move, let him receive added rank or stipend instead.
units.literal: Your servant holds that demotion and promotion should observe fixed yearly limits. If one holds an important post and is not yet due for transfer, add noble rank or salary grade.

units.zh: 其餘進退，宜示遲速之常。
units.en: All other advances and retirements should follow a regular, predictable rhythm.
units.literal: Other advances and retirements should show the normal pace of slow and fast.

units.zh: 若課在中、考如限者，平轉而歷試之，即無茍且之心、滯淹之慮。」
units.en: If a man's review is middling and his term is complete, transfer him in the ordinary course and test him through successive posts. Then no one will grow complacent or fear being left to stagnate."
units.literal: If evaluation is middling and review meets the term, rotate normally and test through successive posts—then there will be no perfunctory mind or fear of stagnation."

units.zh: 五議遺滯，曰：「陛下委宰輔舉才，不遍知也，則訪之庶僚；
units.en: The fifth discourse, on neglected and stalled talent, said: "Your Majesty entrusts the chief ministers with recommending talent. When they do not know enough, inquiry passes to the common officials.
units.literal: The fifth discourse on overlooked and stagnant [talent] said: "Your Majesty entrusts chief ministers to recommend talent. If they do not fully know, inquiry goes to common officials.

units.zh: 又不遍知也，訪之眾人，眾聲囂然，十譽之未信，一毀之可疑。
units.en: When they still do not know enough, inquiry passes to the crowd. Then the voices grow clamorous: ten praises win no trust, while one slander breeds suspicion.
units.literal: If still not fully known, inquiry goes to the multitude—the voices clamor; ten praises are not believed, one slander raises doubt.

units.zh: 臣謂宜采士論，以譽多者先用，非大故者勿棄。」
units.en: I hold that the court should heed scholarly opinion, appoint first those most widely praised, and not discard men who have no grave fault."
units.literal: Your servant holds that one should take up scholars' opinions, using first those with the most praise, and not abandon those without grave fault."

units.zh: 六議藩府官屬，曰：「諸使辟署，務得才以重府望，能否已試，則引而置之朝，無俾久滯。」
units.en: The sixth discourse, on staff of provincial administrations, said: "When commissioners recruit staff, they should seek real talent to enhance the prestige of their offices. Once a man's ability has been tested, bring him into court service and do not let him languish indefinitely."
units.literal: The sixth discourse on provincial staff said: "When various commissioners recruit staff, they should aim to obtain talent to enhance the prefecture's reputation. Once ability has been tested, bring them to court appointments—do not let them long stagnate."

units.zh: 帝皆然之，下詔褒答。
units.en: The emperor agreed with every point and issued an edict commending and answering him.
units.literal: The emperor approved all and issued an edict of praise in reply.

units.zh: 輔政五年，卒，年六十一。
units.en: He served as chief minister for five years, then died at the age of sixty-one.
units.literal: He assisted in governance five years, then died at age sixty-one.

units.zh: 其息上卒時稿奏，帝悼惜之。
units.en: His son submitted at his death the draft memorial he had been working on, and the emperor mourned him and prized the text.
units.literal: His son presented at his death the draft memorial he had been composing; the emperor mourned and treasured it.

units.zh: 贈太子太傅，謚曰貞憲。
units.en: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhenxian, "Upright and Law-abiding."
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous name was Zhenxian.

units.zh: 憬性清約，位臺宰，而第室童獲猶儒先生家也。
units.en: Jing was by nature austere and frugal. Though he held the highest ministerial office, his house and household were still those of a Confucian gentleman.
units.literal: Jing's nature was pure and frugal. Though occupying the highest ministerial seat, his residence and household retainers were still like a Confucian scholar's home.

units.zh: 得稟入，先建家廟，而竟不營產。
units.en: When he received his stipend he first built a family temple and never, to the end of his life, accumulated property.
units.literal: When he received salary he first built a family temple, and to the end did not amass property.

units.zh: 其鎮湖南也，令孤亙、崔儆並為部刺史，不守法，憬以正彈治之，皆遣客暴憬失於朝。
units.en: While he governed Hunan, Linghu Gen and Cui Jing served as subordinate prefects and broke the law. Jing disciplined them properly, and both sent agents to denounce his misconduct at court.
units.literal: When he governed Hunan, Linghu Gen and Cui Jing were both subordinate prefects and did not observe the law. Jing punished them correctly, and both sent agents to expose Jing's faults at court.

units.zh: 及為相，乃擢儆自大理卿為尚書右丞，亙方貶衢州別駕，引為吉州刺史，人以為賢。
units.en: Once he became chief minister he promoted Cui Jing from director of the Court of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat. Linghu Gen had just been demoted to vice prefect of Quzhou, yet Jing brought him back as prefect of Jizhou, and people judged this magnanimous.
units.literal: When he became chief minister he promoted Cui Jing from Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. Gen had just been demoted to Vice Prefect of Quzhou, and [Zhao Jing] brought him in as Prefect of Jizhou—people regarded this as worthy.

units.zh: 崔造，字玄宰，深州安平人。
units.en: Cui Zao, courtesy name Xuanzai, was a native of Anping in Shen Prefecture.
units.literal: Cui Zao, style Xuanzai, was a native of Anping in Shen Prefecture.

units.zh: 永泰中，與韓會、盧東美、張正則三人友善，居上元，好言當世事，皆自謂王佐才，故號「四夔」。
units.en: During the Yongtai era he was close to Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengze. All four lived in Shangyuan, loved to debate the affairs of the day, and each considered himself fit to serve as a king's right hand, so they were called the "Four Kui."
units.literal: In the Yongtai period he was close friends with Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengze. The four lived in Shangyuan, fond of discussing current affairs, and all called themselves talents fit to assist kings—hence they were styled the "Four Kui."

units.zh: 浙西觀察使李棲筠辟為判官，累遷左司員外郎。
units.en: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Zhexi, recruited him as an administrative aide, and he rose in stages to Vice Director of the Left Office.
units.literal: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun recruited him as administrative aide, and he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Left Office.

units.zh: 與劉晏善，晏得罪，貶信州長史。
units.en: He was on good terms with Liu Yan. When Yan fell from favor, Zao was demoted to chief administrator of Xin Prefecture.
units.literal: He was friendly with Liu Yan. When Yan was convicted, [Zao] was demoted to Chief Administrator of Xin Prefecture.

units.zh: 徙建州刺史。
units.en: He was transferred to prefect of Jian Prefecture.
units.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Jian Prefecture.

units.zh: 朱泚亂，造輒馳檄比州，發所部兵二千以待命，德宗嘉之。
units.en: When Zhu Ci rose in rebellion, Zao at once sent proclamations to neighboring prefectures and mobilized two thousand troops from his command to await orders. Emperor Dezong commended him.
units.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Zao immediately dispatched proclamations to neighboring prefectures, mobilizing two thousand troops from his jurisdiction to await orders. Dezong praised this.

units.zh: 京師平，召還，至藍田，自以舅源休與賊同逆，上疏請罪。
units.en: After the capital was restored he was recalled. When he reached Lantian, considering that his maternal uncle Yuan Xiu had joined the rebels in treason, he submitted a memorial asking to be punished.
units.literal: When the capital was pacified he was summoned back. Reaching Lantian, he considered that his uncle Yuan Xiu had joined the rebels in treason and submitted a memorial requesting punishment.

units.zh: 帝以為有禮，下詔慰勉，擢給事中。
units.en: The emperor judged his conduct honorable, issued an edict to comfort and encourage him, and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: The emperor considered this proper conduct, issued an edict of comfort and encouragement, and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.

units.zh: 貞元二年，以給事中同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In the second year of the Zhenyuan era he was made Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, as Drafting Attendant he became Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

units.zh: 帝謂造敢言，為能立事，故不次用之。
units.en: The emperor said that Zao spoke boldly and could get things done, and therefore promoted him ahead of the usual order.
units.literal: The emperor said Zao dared to speak and could accomplish affairs, and therefore employed him out of turn.

units.zh: 造久在江左，疾錢谷諸使罔上，或幹沒自私，乃建言：「天下兩稅，請委本道觀察使、刺史選官部送京師。
units.en: Zao had long served south of the Yangzi and resented the fiscal commissioners who deceived the throne or seized funds for themselves. He proposed: "The empire's two-tax revenues should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to choose officials and deliver the receipts to the capital.
units.literal: Zao had long been in the Jiangzuo region and resented the grain-finance commissioners who deceived the throne or embezzled for private gain. He memorialized: "The empire's two-tax revenues should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to select officials and deliver them to the capital.

units.zh: 諸道水陸轉運使、度支巡院、江淮轉運使，請悉停，以度支鹽鐵務還尚書省，六曹皆宰相分領。」
units.en: All circuit transport commissioners, expenditure-review patrol offices, and the Jianghuai transport commissioner should be abolished. The expenditure and salt-iron offices should be returned to the Secretariat, with the chief ministers each overseeing one of the six bureaus."
units.literal: The various circuits' land-and-water transport commissioners, expenditure-review patrol offices, and Jianghuai transport commissioner should all be abolished. Return the expenditure and salt-iron affairs to the Secretariat, and let the chief ministers each oversee one of the six bureaus."

units.zh: 於是齊映判兵部，李勉刑部，劉滋吏、禮二部，造戶、工二部；
units.en: Accordingly Qi Ying took charge of the Bureau of War, Li Mian of Punishments, Liu Zi of Personnel and Rites, and Zao of Revenue and Public Works.
units.literal: Thereupon Qi Ying oversaw the Bureau of War, Li Mian the Bureau of Punishments, Liu Zi the Bureaus of Personnel and Rites, and Zao the Bureaus of Revenue and Public Works.

units.zh: 又以戶部侍郎元琇判諸道鹽鐵、榷酒事，吉中孚度支諸道兩稅事。
units.en: Yuan Xiu, Vice Director of Revenue, was also put in charge of salt, iron, and liquor monopolies for all circuits, and Ji Zhongfu was put in charge of the two-tax expenditure for all circuits.
units.literal: Vice Director of Revenue Yuan Xiu was also assigned salt-iron and liquor monopoly affairs for all circuits, and Ji Zhongfu the expenditure affairs of all circuits' two-tax system.

units.zh: 而浙江東、西歲入米七十五萬石，方歲饑，更以兩稅準米百萬，豪、壽、洪、潭二十萬，責韓滉杜亞漕送東渭橋。
units.en: Zhejiang East and West had previously delivered 750,000 shi of grain each year. In a year of famine the quota was raised to the two-tax equivalent of one million shi, with Hao, Shou, Hong, and Tan together supplying 200,000. Han Huang and Du Ya were ordered to transport the grain by canal to Dongwei Bridge.
units.literal: Zhejiang East and West had annually delivered 750,000 shi of grain. In a year of famine the quota was changed to a two-tax equivalent of 1,000,000 shi of grain, with Hao, Shou, Hong, and Tan contributing 200,000. Han Huang and Du Ya were charged to transport by canal to Dongwei Bridge.

units.zh: 諸道有鹽鐵處，仍置巡院。
units.en: In circuits where salt and iron were produced, patrol offices were still retained.
units.literal: Where circuits had salt-iron [production], patrol offices were still established.

units.zh: 歲盡，宰相計最殿以聞。
units.en: At the end of the year the chief ministers calculated the best and worst results and reported them to the throne.
units.literal: At year's end the chief ministers calculated best and worst grades and reported them.

units.zh: 造厚元琇，故首命之。
units.en: Zao was on close terms with Yuan Xiu and therefore gave him the leading appointment.
units.literal: Zao was close to Yuan Xiu, and therefore appointed him first.

units.zh: 時滉方領轉運，有寵於帝，朝廷仰其須。
units.en: At the time Han Huang was still in charge of transport and enjoyed the emperor's favor; the court depended on him for supplies.
units.literal: At the time Huang was just leading transport and was favored by the emperor; the court relied on his supplies.

units.zh: 滉持不可改，帝重違之，復以滉滉為江淮轉運使，余如造請。
units.en: Huang insisted the arrangement could not be changed. Unwilling to override him, the emperor restored Han Huang as Jianghuai transport commissioner, while the rest of the plan went forward as Zao had proposed.
units.literal: Huang insisted the plan could not be changed. The emperor was reluctant to oppose him and restored Huang as Jianghuai transport commissioner; the rest followed as Zao had requested.

units.zh: 是秋，江淮米大集，帝美滉功，以滉專領度支諸道鹽鐵、轉運等使。
units.en: That autumn grain from the Jianghuai region poured in. The emperor praised Huang's achievement and put him in sole charge of expenditure, salt and iron, transport, and related offices for all circuits.
units.literal: That autumn Jianghuai grain assembled in great quantity. The emperor praised Huang's achievement and had Huang solely direct expenditure, all circuits' salt-iron affairs, transport, and other commissioners.

units.zh: 造懼，始托疾辭位，乃罷為太子右庶子，貶琇雷州司戶參軍。
units.en: Alarmed, Zao first pleaded illness to resign. He was removed to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household, and Yuan Xiu was demoted to revenue officer of Lei Prefecture.
units.literal: Zao feared this. He first pleaded illness to resign and was then dismissed to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household; Xiu was demoted to Revenue Officer of Lei Prefecture.

units.zh: 於是造所請悉罷，以憂愧卒，年五十一。
units.en: Everything Zao had proposed was then undone. He died of grief and shame at the age of fifty-one.
units.literal: Thereupon all Zao had requested was abolished. He died of grief and shame at age fifty-one.

units.zh: 議者謂造舉不適時，方用之乏，不能權濟大事，雖據舊典，奚能抗一切之制雲。
units.en: Later critics said Zao's proposals came at the wrong moment: just when supplies were desperately needed, he could not maneuver flexibly on a matter of state. However sound his precedents, he was in no position to overturn a system that controlled everything.
units.literal: Commentators said Zao's proposals were ill-timed—just when supplies were needed he could not flexibly manage great affairs. Though based on old precedents, how could he resist an all-controlling system?

units.zh: 齊映，瀛州高陽人。
units.en: Qi Ying was a native of Gaoyang in Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Qi Ying was a native of Gaoyang in Ying Prefecture.

units.zh: 舉進士，博學宏詞，中之，補河南府參軍事。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric examination, then was appointed military adjutant of Henan Prefecture.
units.literal: He passed the Jinshi examination and the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric tests, and was appointed Henan Prefecture military adjutant.

units.zh: 滑亳節度使令狐彰署掌書記，彰疾甚，引映托後事。
units.en: Linghu Zhang, military commissioner of Hua and Bo, appointed him chief secretary. When Zhang fell gravely ill he entrusted his affairs after death to Ying.
units.literal: Hua-Bo Military Commissioner Linghu Zhang appointed him chief secretary. When Zhang was gravely ill he entrusted Ying with affairs after his death.

units.zh: 映因說彰納節，歸諸子京師。
units.en: Ying then persuaded Zhang to surrender his command and send his sons to the capital.
units.literal: Ying thereupon persuaded Zhang to surrender his commission and send his sons to the capital.

units.zh: 彰從之，即以女妻映。
units.en: Zhang agreed and gave Ying his daughter in marriage.
units.literal: Zhang complied and gave his daughter to Ying in marriage.

units.zh: 彰卒，軍亂，映間歸東都。
units.en: When Zhang died the army mutinied, and Ying made his way back to the eastern capital.
units.literal: When Zhang died the army mutinied, and Ying slipped away back to the eastern capital.

units.zh: 三城使馬燧辟為判官。
units.en: Ma Sui, commissioner of the Three Cities, recruited him as an administrative aide.
units.literal: Three Cities Commissioner Ma Sui recruited him as administrative aide.

units.zh: 盧杞薦授刑部員外郎。
units.en: Lu Qi recommended him, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments.
units.literal: Lu Qi recommended him and he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments.

units.zh: 又為鳳翔張鎰判官。
units.en: He later served as administrative aide to Zhang Yi in Fengxiang.
units.literal: He also served as administrative aide to Zhang Yi of Fengxiang.

units.zh: 映練軍事，論奏數稱旨，進行軍司馬。
units.en: Ying was skilled in military affairs, and his memorials often pleased the emperor, who promoted him to army vice marshal.
units.literal: Ying was versed in military affairs; his submitted discussions often pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Army Vice Marshal.

units.zh: 會德宗出奉天，鎰儒緩不知兵，部將李楚琳者，素慓悍，欲介賊為亂。
units.en: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Zhang Yi was a bookish man, slow-moving and ignorant of war. A subordinate general named Li Chulin was naturally fierce and unruly and wanted to join the rebels in raising trouble.
units.literal: When Dezong fled to Fengtian, Yi was a Confucian, slow and ignorant of warfare. A subordinate general, Li Chulin, was by nature fierce and unruly and wished to collude with the rebels to raise disorder.

units.zh: 映與齊抗請先事誅之，鎰不用，更示寬大，徐謂楚琳曰：「欲以君使外，若何？」
units.en: Ying and Qi Kang urged that Chulin be killed first. Yi refused and instead tried a show of leniency, saying slowly to Chulin: "I would like to send you on assignment elsewhere. What do you say?"
units.literal: Ying and Qi Kang asked to execute him preemptively. Yi did not adopt this, instead showing leniency, and slowly said to Chulin: "I wish to send you abroad on mission—what do you think?"

units.zh: 楚琳恐，夜殺鎰以應賊，映雅為軍中慕賴，故得免。
units.en: Chulin grew afraid. That night he killed Yi and went over to the rebels. Ying had long been respected and trusted in the army, and so he escaped unharmed.
units.literal: Chulin feared this. By night he killed Yi to join the rebels. Ying had long been trusted and relied upon in the army, and therefore escaped harm.

units.zh: 奔奉天，授御史中丞。
units.en: He fled to Fengtian and was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: He fled to Fengtian and was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 從幸梁，道險澀，常為帝禦。
units.en: On the emperor's journey to Liang the road was dangerous and rough, and Ying constantly drove the carriage for him.
units.literal: Following the emperor's journey to Liang, the road was treacherous and rough, and he constantly drove for the emperor.

units.zh: 會馬駭突，帝恐傷映，詔舍轡，固不去，曰：「馬奔踶，不過傷臣；
units.en: Once the horses bolted in fright. Fearing Ying would be hurt, the emperor told him to let go of the reins, but he refused to leave, saying: "If the horses rear and kick, they can hurt me at most.
units.literal: When horses bolted in alarm the emperor feared Ying would be hurt and ordered him to drop the reins. He firmly would not leave, saying: "If the horses rear and kick, at most they injure your servant.

units.zh: 舍之，或犯清蹕，臣雖死不中償責。」
units.en: If I drop the reins they may break the imperial procession. Even if I die, that would not atone for such a fault."
units.literal: If I abandon them they might violate the imperial procession—though your servant dies it would not repay the debt."

units.zh: 帝嘉嘆，擢給事中。
units.en: The emperor praised him warmly and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: The emperor praised and sighed, and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.

units.zh: 映為人白晰長大，言音鴻爽，故帝常令侍左右，或前馬臚傳詔旨。
units.en: Ying was fair-complexioned, tall, and imposing, with a clear, ringing voice. The emperor therefore kept him close at hand and sometimes had him ride ahead as herald to proclaim edicts.
units.literal: Ying was fair-skinned, tall, and large; his speech was resonant and clear. Therefore the emperor often had him attend at his side, sometimes riding ahead as herald to announce edicts.

units.zh: 進中書舍人。
units.en: He was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer.
units.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer.

units.zh: 貞元二年，以舍人同中書門下平章事，俄改中書侍郎，封河間縣男，與崔造、劉滋並輔政。
units.en: In the second year of the Zhenyuan era he became Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as drafting officer. Soon he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Hejian County, and shared governance with Cui Zao and Liu Zi.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, as drafting officer he became Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery. Soon he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Hejian County, and assisted in governance together with Cui Zao and Liu Zi.

units.zh: 滋端重寡言，映謙不肯事否可，一顓於造。
units.en: Liu Zi was grave and sparing of speech. Ying was deferential and unwilling to settle matters on his own; everything turned on Zao.
units.literal: Zi was dignified and taciturn. Ying was modest and unwilling to decide yes or no—everything focused on Zao.

units.zh: 會造疾，映乃當國。
units.en: When Zao fell ill, Ying took charge of the government.
units.literal: When Zao fell ill, Ying then controlled the state.

units.zh: 吐蕃數入寇，關輔震騷，鹹言帝欲避狄。
units.en: The Tibetans raided repeatedly, throwing the Guanzhong region into alarm, and rumor spread that the emperor meant to flee before the barbarians.
units.literal: Tibet repeatedly raided inward; Guanfu was shaken with alarm, and everywhere it was said the emperor wished to flee the barbarians.

units.zh: 映入諫曰：「戎狄不懲，臣之罪也。
units.en: Ying went in to remonstrate, saying: "If the barbarians go unpunished, the fault is mine.
units.literal: Ying entered to remonstrate, saying: "If the barbarians are not punished, it is your servant's fault.

units.zh: 然內外恟恟，謂陛下具糗糧，欲治行。
units.en: Yet inside and outside the court people are terrified, saying that Your Majesty has gathered provisions and is preparing to depart.
units.literal: Yet inside and outside are panicked, saying Your Majesty has prepared dry rations and intends to set out on a journey.

units.zh: 夫大幸不再，奈何不與臣等計乎？」
units.en: Good fortune does not strike twice. Why not discuss this with us?"
units.literal: Great fortune does not come twice—why not consult with your servants?"

units.zh: 因俯伏流涕，天子為感寤。
units.en: He then prostrated himself and wept, and the emperor was deeply moved.
units.literal: He then prostrated himself weeping, and the Son of Heaven was moved to awakening.

units.zh: 後給事中袁高忤帝旨，而映以為尚書左丞、御史大夫。
units.en: Later, when Drafting Attendant Yuan Gao offended the emperor, Ying was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Later Drafting Attendant Yuan Gao offended the emperor's intent, and Ying was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 始，映微時，張延賞遇之善。
units.en: In Ying's early days, when he was still unknown, Zhang Yanshang had treated him kindly.
units.literal: Initially, when Ying was obscure, Zhang Yanshang treated him well.

units.zh: 及映相，而延賞為左仆射，數為映畫事，又為所親求官，映不答，延賞恚。
units.en: Once Ying became chief minister while Yanshang served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yanshang often drafted business for him and also asked favors for his friends. Ying gave no answer, and Yanshang grew furious.
units.literal: When Ying became chief minister and Yanshang was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yanshang often drafted affairs for Ying and also sought offices for his intimates. Ying did not respond, and Yanshang was enraged.

units.zh: 既復用，即劾映非宰相器。
units.en: When Yanshang returned to power he at once impeached Ying as unfit for the chancellorship.
units.literal: Once restored to power he immediately impeached Ying as unfit to be chief minister.

units.zh: 明年，貶夔州刺史，徙衡州。
units.en: The next year Ying was demoted to prefect of Kuizhou and later transferred to Hengzhou.
units.literal: The next year [Ying] was demoted to Prefect of Kui Prefecture and then transferred to Heng Prefecture.

units.zh: 久之，為桂管、江西兩觀察使。
units.en: After some years he served as observation commissioner of Guiguan and Jiangxi.
units.literal: After a long time he became observation commissioner of both Guiguan and Jiangxi.

units.zh: 始，映罷不以罪，冀復進，乃掊斂獻貢，以中帝欲。
units.en: At first Ying had not been dismissed for any crime, and he hoped to return to court. He therefore squeezed the region for tribute to satisfy the emperor's wishes.
units.literal: Initially when Ying was dismissed it was not for crime; he hoped to advance again and therefore extorted and collected tribute to hit the emperor's desires.

units.zh: 初，諸藩銀大瓶止五尺，李兼為江西，始獻六尺瓶，至映乃八尺雲。
units.en: At first the great silver vases presented by the various prefectures were only five chi tall. When Li Jian governed Jiangxi he was the first to send six-chi vases; by Ying's time they had reached eight chi.
units.literal: At first among the various prefectures silver great vases were only five chi. When Li Jian governed Jiangxi he first presented six-chi vases; by Ying's time they reached eight chi.

units.zh: 卒，年四十八，贈禮部尚書，謚曰忠。
units.en: He died at the age of forty-eight. He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Zhong, "Loyal."
units.literal: He died at age forty-eight. He was posthumously granted Minister of Rites; his posthumous name was Zhong.

units.zh: 盧邁，字子玄，河南河南人。
units.en: Lu Mai, courtesy name Zixuan, was a native of Henan in Henan.
units.literal: Lu Mai, style Zixuan, was a native of Henan in Henan.

units.zh: 性孝友。
units.en: He was filial and brotherly by nature.
units.literal: His nature was filial and fraternal.

units.zh: 舉明經入第，補太子正字。
units.en: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed corrector in the Heir Apparent's household.
units.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Corrector in the Heir Apparent's household.

units.zh: 以拔萃調河南主簿、集賢校理。
units.en: Selected through the bawei examination, he was appointed chief clerk of Henan and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
units.literal: Through the bawei selection he was assigned as Chief Clerk of Henan and Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

units.zh: 公卿交薦之，擢右補闕。
units.en: Dukes and ministers recommended him in turn, and he was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor.
units.literal: Dukes and ministers jointly recommended him; he was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor.

units.zh: 三遷吏部員外郎。
units.en: He was transferred three times until he reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Three transfers to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 以族屬客江介，出為滁州刺史。
units.en: Because his clan had been guests in the Jiang region, he was sent out as prefect of Chu Prefecture.
units.literal: Because his clan served as guests in the Jiang region he went out as Prefect of Chu Prefecture.

units.zh: 召還，再遷諫議大夫。
units.en: He was recalled to the capital and promoted twice to Remonstrance Grandee.
units.literal: Summoned back, twice transferred to Remonstrance Grandee.

units.zh: 數條當世病利，進給事中。
units.en: He repeatedly set forth the ills and benefits of the age and was promoted to Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: Several times he listed the ills and benefits of the age; he was promoted to Drafting Attendant.

units.zh: 俄會考課，邁以不滿歲，固辭上考，薦紳高其讓。
units.en: Soon the merit review came due. Mai had not served a full year and firmly declined the top grade; the gentry admired his modesty.
units.literal: Soon there was merit review; Mai had not completed a full year and firmly declined the top grade; the gentry esteemed his yielding.

units.zh: 改尚書右丞。
units.en: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: He was changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 將作監元亙攝祠，以私忌不聽誓，御史劾之。
units.en: Yuan Gen, Director of Palace Construction, was acting as substitute sacrificer and, citing a private taboo day, refused to hear the oath. The censor impeached him.
units.literal: Director of Palace Construction Yuan Gen acted as substitute for sacrifice and on a private taboo day would not hear the oath; the censor impeached him.

units.zh: 帝疑其罰，下尚書省議。
units.en: The emperor doubted whether the penalty was right and referred the case to the Department of State Affairs for deliberation.
units.literal: The emperor doubted the punishment and referred it to the Department of State Affairs for discussion.

units.zh: 邁曰：「按大夫士將祭於公，既視濯而父母死，猶奉祭。
units.en: Mai said: "According to the rites, when a grandee or scholar is about to sacrifice on behalf of the lord, even if after the purifying wash his parents die, he still carries out the sacrifice.
units.literal: Mai said: "According to the rites, when a grandee or scholar is about to sacrifice for the lord, if after the purifying wash the parents die, he still offers sacrifice.

units.zh: 禮，散齊有大功喪，致齊有期喪，齊有疾病，聽還舍，不奉祭。
units.en: The rites provide that during dispersed fasting, if there is mourning for a close relative, one does not sacrifice; during concentrated fasting, if there is mourning for a lesser relative, one does not sacrifice; and if illness occurs during fasting, one may return home and not sacrifice.
units.literal: In ritual, during dispersed fasting if there is mourning for a close relative, during concentrated fasting if there is mourning for a lesser relative, during fasting if there is illness—one may return home and not offer sacrifice.

units.zh: 無忌日不受誓者。
units.en: Nowhere do the rites allow one to refuse the oath on a taboo day.
units.literal: There is no provision for not accepting the oath on a taboo day.

units.zh: 雖令忌日與告，且《春秋》不以家事辭王事，今攝祭特命也，亙以常令拒特命，執非所宜。」
units.en: Even if regulations allow taboo days to coincide with leave, the Spring and Autumn Annals never permits family affairs to refuse the king's business. The substitute sacrifice today is a special command. Gen used ordinary regulations to refuse a special command; such adherence is not appropriate."
units.literal: Though orders may align taboo days with leave, moreover the Spring and Autumn Annals does not let family affairs refuse the king's affairs—now the substitute sacrifice is a special command; Gen used ordinary regulations to refuse a special command—his adherence is not appropriate."

units.zh: 遂抵罪。
units.en: Gen was therefore found guilty.
units.literal: He was therefore convicted.

units.zh: 以本官同中書門下平章事。
units.en: He was made Co-Chancellor while retaining his original office.
units.literal: With his original office he was made Co-Chancellor.

units.zh: 進中書侍郎。
units.en: He was promoted to Vice President of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He advanced to Vice President of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 時陸贄、趙憬專大政，邁居中，治身循法無它過。
units.en: At that time Lu Zhi and Zhao Jing monopolized major policy. Mai stood between them and conducted himself by the law without other fault.
units.literal: At that time Lu Zhi and Zhao Jing monopolized major policy; Mai stood in the middle, governing himself by law without other fault.

units.zh: 久之，暴眩省中，輿還第。
units.en: After some time he suddenly fainted in the Secretariat and was carried home in a litter.
units.literal: After a long time he suddenly suffered dizziness in the Secretariat and was carried back to his mansion.

units.zh: 詔大臣即問，固乞骸骨，罷為太子賓客。
units.en: The emperor ordered senior ministers to visit him at once. Mai firmly asked to retire on account of age and was dismissed as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: The emperor ordered great ministers to visit and inquire; he firmly begged to retire on old bones and was dismissed as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 卒，年六十，贈太子太傅。
units.en: He died at the age of sixty and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He died at sixty, posthumously Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 邁每有功、緦喪，必容稱其服，而情有加焉。
units.en: Whenever Mai observed mourning for a close or distant relative, he always wore the proper garments with fitting ease, yet showed extra feeling beyond the form.
units.literal: Whenever Mai observed mourning of the gong grade or the si grade, he always accommodated himself to the proper garments, yet showed extra feeling.

units.zh: 叔下邽令休沐過家，邁終日與群子姓均指使，無位貌之異。
units.en: When his uncle, the magistrate of Xiaji, took leave to visit the family home, Mai spent the whole day directing the gathered cousins and gave orders equally, with no difference of rank or appearance.
units.literal: When his uncle, magistrate of Xiaji, took leave to visit home, Mai spent the whole day directing the gathered cousins equally without difference in rank or appearance.

units.zh: 再娶無子，或勸畜姬媵，對曰：「兄弟之子，猶子也，可以主後。」
units.en: He remarried but had no sons. Some urged him to take concubines. He replied: "A brother's son is like one's own son and can continue the line."
units.literal: He remarried but had no sons; some urged him to keep concubines. He replied: "A brother's son is like one's own son and can continue the line."

units.zh: 所得稟賜，皆賑姻舊之乏。
units.en: Whatever stipends and gifts he received he used to relieve needy kin and old friends.
units.literal: Whatever stipends and gifts he received he used to relieve needy kin and friends.

units.zh: 其從父弟禋喪還洛陽，過都，邁奏請往哭之，盡哀。
units.en: When his cousin Yin returned from mourning to Luoyang and passed through the capital, Mai memorialized to go and weep for him, mourning to the full extent of the rites.
units.literal: When his paternal cousin Yin returned from mourning to Luoyang and passed through the capital, Mai memorialized to go weep for him and mourned to the full.

units.zh: 時執政自以宰相尊，五服皆不過從問吊，而邁獨不徇時，議者重其仁而亮雲。
units.en: At that time the ruling officials considered themselves too lofty as chancellors: for mourning within the five degrees of kinship they never went in person but only sent followers to inquire. Mai alone would not follow the fashion. Critics valued his humanity and candor.
units.literal: The ruling officials considered themselves lofty as chancellors; for all mourning within five degrees of kin they only sent followers to inquire and condole—but Mai alone would not follow the fashion; critics valued his humanity and candor.

units.zh: 贊曰：楊綰之德，陸贄之賢，而袞、憬以為憎，何哉？
units.en: The appraiser says: Yang Guan had virtue and Lu Zhi had talent—yet Chang Gun and Zhao Jing resented them. Why?
units.literal: The appraiser says: Yang Guan's virtue, Lu Zhi's worthiness—yet Gun and Jing were jealous of them; why?

units.zh: 士固蔽於娼前，然主聽不一，故乘以為奸。
units.en: Scholars are indeed blinded before flatterers, but when the sovereign's ear is not single-minded, they seize the chance for treachery.
units.literal: Scholars are indeed blinded before flatterers, but when the sovereign's hearing is not one, they therefore seize opportunity for treachery.

units.zh: 昔齊桓、秦堅任管仲、王猛，興區區，霸天下，蓋不以不肖者參之。
units.en: In former times Duke Huan of Qi and Emperor Jian of Qin entrusted Guan Zhong and Wang Meng. From a small realm each dominated the world, largely because they did not let unworthy men share in power.
units.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi and Emperor Jian of Qin entrusted Guan Zhong and Wang Meng—with only a small realm they dominated the world, largely because they did not mix in the unworthy.

units.zh: 君臣相諒，果難哉！
units.en: For ruler and minister to trust each other in good faith—is it not truly hard!
units.literal: For ruler and minister to trust each other in good faith—is it not truly hard!
